correctness.rationale: Every selected vertex that is isolated in the selected subgraph can be mapped to its rung mate, and every nonisolated selected vertex to an external private neighbor. Neither assignments of the same kind nor mixed assignments can coincide, so |D|≤n; an entire row attains this. At size n, full and empty columns are equinumerous. Only empty columns can supply external private neighbors to full columns, and each empty vertex must be used, which forbids neighboring singleton columns. Full columns cannot touch singleton columns either, since the latter would then have no private neighbor. With only singletons, a selected interior vertex loses its private neighbor exactly when one adjacent column selects its row and the other the opposite row; period two is necessary and sufficient, including the vacuous constraint at n=2. With only full and empty columns every column meets exactly one unlike neighbor, so these edges are the unique perfect matching of the even column path. This gives exactly the stated words. The two checkerboards are the only independent words, and complementing pairs the extremizers.
residual_risks: The separate replay exhausts all size-n subsets for 2≤n≤10 and obtains 46 extremizers in total; it does not check larger n or replace the injection and structural proof. The phrase ‘prior neighbor’ in Step 3 is a typographical error for ‘private neighbor’.
